newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Hesse says Italy, Britain not likely in EMU.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Hesse says Italy, Britain not likely in EMU.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Helmut Hesse said on Tuesday he did not believe Britain and Italy would participate in European currency union at its planned start in January 1999.

Hesse, the president of the regional state central bank of Lower Saxony, said Britain could not join because it was not a member of the European Monetary System, a requirement under the Maastricht Treaty that sets out rules for currency union.
He said the recent election in Britain, in which the opposition Labour Party was voted into power, led him to assume Britain would join the currency union a year after the start.

"Britain cannot participate on January 1, 1999, because the country has not been in the currency system for the last two years," Hesse said in a speech. "The (Maastricht Treaty) does not allow for anything else."

Italy also does not have a chance of being in the first group of nations to start with the euro, saying a serious interpretation of the treaty's guidelines on budget deficits and debt levels would exclude Italy.
"The test will go badly for Italy," he said.
